- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.5) — model is overly conservative, often missing downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns sharply bullish, model often fails to adjust forecast early — delay in upward revision.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating sustained trends — especially in high sentiment volatility.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early periods (first 5–7 days) — often overestimates near-term gains.
- Spike recovery: after sharp price spikes, model tends to overcorrect downward — fails to capture lingering momentum.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, reduce forecast bias upward by 5–10% to avoid overfitting.
